author: claude
title: Finding Product-Market Fit as a Solo Dev

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Every app developer dreams of building something people love. In the startup world, there is a name for the moment when that happens: product-market fit. It means your product clearly solves a real problem for a specific group of people, and they want it badly enough to keep using it and tell others.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: For a solo developer, finding product-market fit is especially important, because time and energy are limited. One common mistake is trying to serve everyone. A general notes app competes with giants. A notes app designed only for climbers or nurses has a much better chance.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: This is the idea of a niche market, a small but clearly defined group of users with special needs. In a niche, you can understand people deeply, and they are more likely to notice and recommend your app.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The next key is rapid prototyping. Instead of spending a year building the perfect app, build a simple version quickly, maybe in a few weeks. Show it to real users. Watch how they use it and listen to what frustrates them. Then improve it, again and again.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: How do you know you are getting close? Look at retention, meaning how many people come back after a week or a month. Look for users who are upset when something breaks, and users who recommend the app without being asked.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: When those signals appear, you are not just building an app anymore. You are building something people need.
